C-01.note: Demo case A. Fake Microsoft 365 password-expiry notice with a blocklisted link.

C-02.note: Demo case B. Bank-detail change from a one-character lookalike of Dana's real vendor. Simulation flag on.
C-02.user_reason: That's Apex, we pay them every month.

C-03.note: Demo case C. Real invoice from Dana's real vendor with a clean portal link.

C-04.note: Payroll diversion to HR from a lookalike of the company domain. Simulation flag on.

C-05.note: Executive gift-card request from personal webmail: the classic CEO-fraud pattern. Clean domain, but content signals are clear.
red_flags: gift card purchase with codes by email
C-05.user_reason: Elena emails from her personal account when she travels.

C-06.note: Failed-delivery notice with a blocklisted link and a small payment demand.
C-06.user_reason: I'm expecting samples from a supplier this week.

C-07.note: Real benefits vendor, known to Marcus, clean portal link, no request for money or data.

C-08.note: Internal meeting agenda from a coworker on the company domain with a clean intranet link.

C-09.note: First-contact vendor with an unknown domain asking for billing details. Truly legitimate, risky-looking.
red_flags: request for billing details from a first-contact vendor
C-09.user_reason: We met them at the expo last month and I asked for the catalog.

C-10.note: Known vendor's real domain sends an odd bank-change request. Truly phishing (compromised mailbox), clean sender evidence.

C-11.note: Held-out Kaggle phishing row 1 (pharmacy spam), original text. Synthetic From on a newly registered malicious domain, no links.

C-12.note: Held-out Kaggle phishing row 2 (pharmacy spam), original text. Synthetic From on a newly registered malicious domain, no links.
C-12.user_reason: I thought it was one of the pharmacy discount offers we get through our benefits provider.

C-13.note: Held-out Kaggle phishing row 3 (word-salad spam, classifier 0.655), original text. Synthetic From on a newly registered malicious domain, no links.

C-14.note: MFA reset from a one-character lookalike of the company domain, link on the same lookalike. Simulation flag on.
red_flags: asks for password and MFA code
C-14.user_reason: IT said everyone has to set up MFA again this month.

C-15.note: Voicemail notice that asks for a Microsoft 365 sign-in on a blocklisted link. Simulation flag on.

C-16.note: Held-out Kaggle legitimate row 1 (vacation notice), original text. Synthetic From on the company domain, no links.

C-17.note: Held-out Kaggle legitimate row 2 (developer mailing-list post), original text. Synthetic From on a long-standing clean list domain, no links.

C-18.note: Held-out Kaggle legitimate row 3 (internal note on reserves), original text. Synthetic From on the company domain, no links.

C-19.note: Marcus's real payroll vendor posts the Q4 calendar on its clean portal. No request.

C-20.note: Real delivery confirmation from Dana's known carrier with a clean tracking link. Contrast with E-006.

C-21.note: Known customer asks Priya for a quote. Clean known domain, no links, no money or credential request.

C-22.note: Real IT maintenance notice from the company domain. No links, no request. Contrast with E-014.

C-23.note: Shared-document lure from a known customer's real domain (compromised mailbox). Link host unknown. Truly phishing, clean-looking.
red_flags: shared document from an external sender

C-24.note: CFO's real internal address (compromised mailbox) asks AP to pay a new payee, skipping vendor setup. Truly phishing, clean sender evidence.
red_flags: payment to a payee not in vendor records
deadline tied to the payment run
C-24.user_reason: Rob is our CFO and he sends me sponsorship invoices to add to the run all the time.

C-25.note: Known customer domain with reply-to on personal webmail, asking for staff contact details (BEC reconnaissance). Truly phishing. Same evidence shape as E-030, which is legitimate.

C-26.note: Unsolicited recruiter with an unknown domain and link (malware lure). Truly phishing. Same evidence shape as E-009, which is legitimate.
red_flags: unsolicited first contact with files to open
C-26.user_reason: We're hiring for the warehouse and I've been posting on job boards.

C-27.note: Real trade-show marketing email with countdown urgency and a payment ask. Sender and link not in threat intel. Truly legitimate, risky-looking.

C-28.note: Marcus's real payroll vendor asks for an annual admin sign-in on a subdomain not in threat intel. Truly legitimate, risky-looking.
red_flags: unknown link on a vendor subdomain
sign-in request with an access-pause deadline
C-28.user_reason: PayWell makes us re-verify admin access every year before W-2 season.

C-29.note: Real internal finance announcement asking staff to create an account on a new third-party tool. Link not in threat intel. Truly legitimate, risky-looking.
C-29.user_reason: Finance announced the new expense tool at the all-hands.

C-30.note: Known customer's real domain with reply-to on personal webmail during a mail migration. Truly legitimate. Same evidence shape as E-025, which is phishing.
red_flags: request to send business data to a personal address
